scope: Preparation and limited source triage for Chemistry1.25; not reaction coverage certification or teaching completion.

decisions.judgement: Arrangement, movement and energy in states describe particles, without naming an additional chemical reaction.
Interconversions are physical state changes; unchanged substance/state notation is not a new chemical-reaction family.
Own statement specifies dilution and gas diffusion observations, without prescribing a named reagent reaction. Any chosen reacting demonstration needs a separate reaction link, for example3.18.
Solvent, solute, solution and saturated-solution definitions do not prescribe an additional chemical equation.
Solubility units per100gsolvent are a physical quantity, not a named chemical reaction.
Plotting/interpreting solubility curves introduces no named chemical-reaction equation.
Specified solubility investigation does not name a new reacting reagent pair. Dissolving energetic examples are reviewed separately under3.2/3.8.
Element/compound/mixture classification does not itself prescribe a particular synthesis/decomposition reaction.
Melting/boiling purity evidence concerns physical behaviour, without naming an additional chemical equation.
Five specified separation techniques separate mixtures; these are not chemical cracking or new reacting-product requirements.
Chromatogram composition evidence does not prescribe a chemical-reaction equation.
Rf calculation/identification is a separation measurement rather than a new chemical-reaction family.
Ink/food-colour chromatography practical does not prescribe a reacting reagent pair.
Atom/molecule definitions do not name a chemical reaction.
Subatomic particle locations/masses/charges are structure knowledge, not a separately named reaction.
Atomic/mass number, isotope and relative-mass definitions do not prescribe a named reaction.
Abundance-weighted mass calculation is not a chemical-reaction equation.
Atomic-number/group/period ordering does not itself prescribe a reaction.
First20 atom electronic configurations are distinct from a separately required ion-transfer half-equation.
Metal/nonmetal classification byposition does not prescribe an extra named reaction.
Main-group configurations linked toposition do not prescribe an extra chemical-reaction family.

explicitlyDeferred.reason: Acid-base character of oxides needs cross-topic reaction-family review; do not exclude from1.25 only because this point names no particular oxide.

limitations: Arrow-bearing rows are not unique reactions or proof of correct word/formula/state equations. Absence of an arrow is not proof of missing explanation.
